HomePage.heroEyebrow: Vendor matching, checked pair by pair
HomePage.heroTitleLead: Check whether your matching tool merged the wrong people —
HomePage.heroBody: PairSight compares a vendor’s matching decisions with careful pair-by-pair assessments, so you can see each vendor’s precision and recall tradeoff and inspect every disagreement.
HomePage.howTitle: From two exports to a clear verdict, in three steps
HomePage.howBody: Bring the records and what each vendor matched. Say what counts as the same person. Jev judges every pair that matters, and PairSight lines the verdicts up against each vendor.
HomePage.lookTitle: Every number traces back to a pair you can open
HomePage.look1Body: Open a pair to see both records side by side, what differs, Jev’s score and each vendor’s decision.
HomePage.look2Body: The Runs centre keeps each run with exactly what it was run with: rules, fields, threshold, model and vendors.
HomePage.look3Body: Choose the match threshold before you see results, so a run’s numbers never shift after the fact.
HomePage.step1Body: Upload the original customer records and each vendor’s matching export, in pair or group format.
HomePage.step2Title: Decide what counts as a match
HomePage.step2Body: Describe when two records are the same individual, and choose which records are worth comparing.
HomePage.step3Body: Jev assesses every candidate pair. PairSight lines its judgments up against each vendor’s decisions.
HomePage.limitsBody: Results are a way to find and inspect problems, not a certificate of accuracy.
HomePage.limit1Body: Precision and recall compare vendors with Jev’s judgments. Jev can be wrong — inspect any pair and use your own judgment.
HomePage.limit2Body: Pairs outside your rules that no vendor matched aren’t assessed, so duplicates among them stay unseen.
HomePage.limit3Body: One vendor may merge more carefully while another finds more duplicates. You decide which tradeoff fits.
HomePage.ctaTitle: Run your first evaluation on your own records.
HomePage.ctaBody: Start with your records and one vendor’s export. Or look around the sandbox first: no account needed.
HomePage.footer: Pairs are judged by Jev, TypeSafe’s AI

Rules.title: Rules
Rules.description: Define what counts as the same individual, then choose which records are worth comparing.
Rules.thresholdDescription: How sure Jev must be for a pair to count as a PairSight match. Jev scores every pair the same way; this only sets where the line is drawn. The next run keeps it.
Rules.thresholdNote_lenient: Borderline pairs count as matches: finds more likely duplicates, at the risk of more wrong merges.
Rules.thresholdNote_balanced: The default. In testing, clearly different people scored 0.11 or less and the same people 0.76 or more, so {value} sits in the gap.
Rules.thresholdNote_strict: Only pairs Jev is confident about count: fewer wrong merges, more duplicates left unmatched.
Rules.thresholdNote_custom: Pairs Jev scores at or above {value} count as a match.
Rules.identityTitle: What makes two records the same individual?
Rules.identityDescription: Jev reads these instructions for every pair it assesses. Plain language works best.
Rules.sameRequired: Describe what counts as the same individual.
Rules.countryHint: Helps Jev read names, addresses and phone formats, and reads local phone numbers.
Rules.jevFieldsHint: Only these fields are sent to Jev.
Rules.neverSent: Vendor decisions are never sent to Jev, so its judgment can’t be anchored by them.
Rules.blockingTitle: Choose which records are worth comparing
Rules.blockingDescription: Comparing every record with every other gets expensive fast. Each rule groups records that share a value into buckets, and only records in the same bucket are compared. Rules overlap — a record can sit in several buckets, but each pair is compared once. Missing values never form a shared bucket.
Rules.noComposites: No composite rules. Combine fields like Last name + Postcode for tighter buckets.
Rules.skipped: {count, plural, one {# record} other {# records}} without a value skipped
Rules.oversized: Oversized bucket: {size, number} records create {pairs, number} pairs. Add a field to split it.
Rules.editorDescription: Records are compared when every selected field matches after normalizing. More fields → smaller, more precise buckets.
Rules.editorPick: Pick one or more fields to preview buckets.
Rules.editorStats: <n>{buckets}</n> shared buckets · <n>{pairs}</n> pairs · largest bucket <n>{largest}</n> records
Rules.summaryOver: {count, number} pairs over the limit. Turn off or tighten a rule.
Rules.summaryOversized: {rule} has a bucket of {size, number} records.
Rules.summaryNote: Every vendor-matched pair is assessed, even outside your rules. Pairs outside both stay unseen.
Rules.blockedSame: Describe what counts as the same individual
Rules.blockedFields: Select at least two fields for assessment
Rules.blockedOver: Reduce pairs to {limit, number} or fewer (now {total, number})
Rules.ruleEmailHint: Trimmed and lowercased; dots and +tags kept
Rules.rulePhoneHint: Converted to international format using the country
Rules.ruleNameHint: Case, spacing and full vs. first + last name normalized
Rules.ruleOverCap: This rule alone creates {pairs, number} pairs; one run allows {limit, number}.
Rules.customDuplicate: A rule with these fields already exists.
Rules.customLimit: You can add up to {max} custom rules.
